summary: Kaniksu National Forest lookout on Kalispell Rock, Pend Oreille County, WA; log cabin and firefinder cab built 1927; cabin ruins remain; no source describes the cab surviving.

facts.design: Log cabin below with a small firefinder cab set on a post atop the summit boulder
facts.status_note: No source describes the firefinder cab surviving. The log cabin survives in part as ruins, and the post hole remains in the summit rock.

visit.trail_note: About 3 miles one way with 1,200 feet of gain per WillhiteWeb. Part of the road is closed; the ridge trail needs some off-trail walking and has had little maintenance. The top needs a short scramble with some exposure.

events.note: Log cabin built; small firefinder cab placed on the summit boulder
Register says last manned in 1935; conflicts with the 1936 newspaper item and WillhiteWeb's c. 1934 date
Wyatt B. Morehead named as lookout on Kalispell in a Colville Examiner item
Lookout put out three small lightning fires in his district (Colville Examiner, August 1936)
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites Register on March 24, 2020

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register says last manned in 1935. WillhiteWeb, citing a Kresek inventory, says no longer used around 1934. A 1936 Colville Examiner item names a lookout here. The story reports all three and does not pick one.

The brief's note lists firelookout.com as standing, but the firelookout.com page we read says Abandoned. Ruins. The Register also says the cabin ruins remain. The story reports the cabin ruins and says no source describes the cab surviving; it does not say the cab was removed.
The Register and Firelookout give 5,276 ft (1,608 m); WillhiteWeb gives 5,278 feet. The record's 1608.1 m matches the 5,276 ft figure, and the difference is about 2 feet.

notes_for_editor: Last-manned date conflicts: Register 1935, WillhiteWeb c. 1934, and a 1936 newspaper item naming Wyatt B. Morehead. The staffed_last 1935 event is kept as the Register's claim and flagged. Brief kind 'tower' may not fit: the structure is a log cabin with a firefinder cab on a post atop a boulder; left unchanged because the kind enum was not checked. Access: the WillhiteWeb access field (most any vehicle) conflicts with its route description (closed road); no source read says whether the public may use the road. Elevation differs by 2 ft between sources. Photos on the Register and WillhiteWeb (Ray Kresek, Gary Weber, Rex Kamstra, Paul Michelson) have unknown licenses, so none added. The 'standing' status in the brief's conflict note was not found on firelookout.com. Fact-check 2026-10-09: removed the claim that the lookout itself is gone; no source read says the firefinder cab is gone or standing. The 'carved' wording was not in the source (WillhiteWeb says 'etched'), and the access wording now matches the route description.
